                                                    DENVER 2, COLORADO


                                                     September 28, 1950




    MEMORAirnUM

    TO:           James Fresques, Presi1ent 1
                  City Council. ~
    FROM:         J. Glenn Donaldso
                  City Attorney.
    SUBJECT:      A Bill for an Ordinance to Publish the Revised
                  Municioal Code of the Ci~ andCounty of Denver.
    The accompanying nine separately bound manuscript volwnes are
    presented to Council by the codification staff.· They represent
    the amended, revised, integrated, and codified law of the City
    and County of Denver of general interest. All new ordinances,
    including the forthcoming sign code and related zoning amend-
/   ment, are incorporated herein. Future ordinances will.have
    to be incorporated into this volume by the publication of
    loose leaf supplements. Advertisement for bids on printing
    i.s currently running in the Daily .J..9..ur~al; the contract is
    available for those who wish to bid on this job. It is hoped
    that within ninety days Denver will have a modern loose leaf
    form Municipal Code not excelled by that of any other city.
    This matter was discussed at the Mayor-Council meeting Wed-
    nesday, September 27, 1950.




    LG-h
    Attachment

                            A BILL

          FOR AN ORDINANCE AMENDING, REVISING,
          CODIFYING, COMPILING I AND RE-ENAC'rING
          THE GENERAL OHDINANCES OF THE CITY
          AND COUNTY OF DENVER, EXCEPT SUCH AS
          AHE SPECIFICALLY SAV1JD HEREIN, PRO-
          VIDING PENALTn:s FOR THE VIOLATION OF
          THE PROVISIONS THERlmF, AND REPEALING
          ALL ORDINANCES OR PAR'l'S OF ORDINANCES
          IN CONFLICT THEREWITH.


     WHEREAS, since the passage of Ordinance No. 156 of the
Series of 1927, being a codified publication of the general
ordinances of the City and County of Denver, many ordinances
of general importance have been passed; and
     WHEREAS, these ordinances are not presently available in
     codified form; and
     WHEREAS, the Council of the City and County of Denver
hereby finds that the existing general ordinances should be
codified, amended, revised, compiled, re-enacted, arranged
analytically in appropriate main divisions, chapters, articles,
and sections, and published as the Revised Municioal Code of
the City and County_of.Denver;
     NOW, THEREFOHE,
BE IT ENACTED BY THE COUNCIL OF 'rHE CITY AND COUNTY OF DENVER:

            • 2.     Amendments.    Any addition or amendment to the Revised

      so that reference to the Revised JY1unicipal Code of the City and County
      of Denver shall be understood as in,,cluding them •
            • 3.     Reference to City Attorney •
            • 3-1.     Examination as to Form.        All bills for ordinances intro-
      duced for passage shall, unless the rules are suspended for their
      passage, be referred to the City Attorney, and it shall be the duty
      of the City Attorney to make an examination thereof and to report
  to the Councilmen, in writing, any irregularity in form thereof, or
  legal objection thereto. /4ec.              /9~1)

  law.     Whenever the word 11 person'' is used in any section of this Re-

                    • 10~    Penalty.   Whenever in any section of this Code or any
           section of a rule or regulation promulgated henmnder the doing of


/x         any act is required, prohibited, or declared to be unlawful and no
           definite fine or penalty is provided for a violation thereof, any
       person, firm, or corporation who shall be convicted of a violation
           of any such section shall, for each offense, be fined in a sum not

       ninety (90) days, or both so fined and imprisoned.
                    The suspension or revocation of any license, certificate evidenc-
           ing accord of inspection services, or other privilege conferred by
           the City shall not be regarded as a penalty for the purposes of this
           Code •

            12', - INITIATIVE, REFERENDUM AND RECALL



      .1.     Unla~f~~_to Sign More Than One Petition.       It shall
hereafter be unlawful for any person in the City and County
of Denver to sign any petition to initiate or refer any
Charter amendment, measure, ordinance, or proposal for a charter
convention, or to sign any petition for the recall of any elec-
tive officer in the City and County of Denver, if said person
has signed a like petition for the same purpose, or without
said person having first fully informed and advised himself
as to the contents of such petition.        It is intended hereby
to make it unlawful for any person to sign more than one
petition for the same purpose, or to sign any petition for
any of said purposes, without being fully informed and ad-
vised as to the contents of the same.        (Sec. 1143)
      .2.     Requirements for Signature§.     Each and every person
signing any such petition, shall be required to make oath,
before a no·tary public or other person authorized to admin-
ister oaths under the laws of the State of Colorado, at the
time of signing thereof, that such person is a qualified
elector of the City and County of Denver, and has not signed
any other or like petition for the same purpose, is fully
acquainted with the subject matter of said petition, and re-
sides at the address accompanying his signature on such petition.
(Sec. 1142)
      .3.     Circulators of Petitions - Dut'.'2; of~   Each and every
circulator of any such petition shall, at or before the time
of filing such petition, make an affidavit in addition to that
required by the Charter o~s~ City and County of Denver, that

  plans, exhibits, and other descriptive matter.                   (Sec.~, Ord. 133,

  structures and facilities constructed thereon and proposed;

  streets, allwys, boulevards, parkways, waterways, airports, and

  ence or envisaged;

  playgrounds, community centers, square, and public buildings
  and structures;

  and extent of roads and right-of-way of public utilities, whether
  publicly or privately owned;
            .3-14(5). Plans for public housing and for the rehabili-
  tation of slums and blighted areas in accordance with the

           .4.      Service Units.   A year's service record shall consist
  of twelve units of service,~.                      A unit of service in the

  month in which the employe shall be paid for a month's service;

  paid working days, but no          more than twelve units of service
  shall be credited to an employe paid by the day, in any cal-
  endar year.            (Sec. 3, Ord. 84, Series of 1946)

      return of agency items, court order, or otherwise, shall be
      initiated by the agency of the City and County through which the
      original receipt was handled.      The head of the agency shall make,
      or cause to be made, a thorough examination into the merits of
      each such refund, shall determine whether it is justified, and
      shall approve or disapprove it •       (Sec. 4, Ord. 171, Series of 1948)
             • 2-5.   Auditor Prescribes Voucher Forms.    For any refund that
      is approved, the head of the agency shall cause to be prepared a
      refund voucher.    'l'he Audi tor shall prescribe the form and content
      of the refund voucher •    (Sec. 5, Ord. 171, Series of 1948)
             . 2-6.   Voucher Transmitted to Auditor for Approval •
             • 2-6(1).   The refund voucher shall be transmitted to the
      Auditor for approval and the issuance of a warrant •
             • 2-6(2).   Refunds shall be charged against the same fund
      to which the original receipt was credited •
             • 2-6(3).   Refunds from the general fund shall be paid out of
      the appropriation ncity Council rv~iscellaneousn or such other appro-
      priation as may hereafter be provided.       (Sec. 6, Ord. 171,·Series
      of 1948)
             .2-7. Where Section 162.2 S~all Not Appll•      This Section

              .1.      Definitions.      When used in this article, ordinances,
      executive orders, orders issued by the Auditor, financial reports,
      and otherwise in connection with the fiscal affairs of the City
      and County of Denver, unless specifically defined otherwise or
      unless the context requires a different meaning, the following
      terms shall have the following meanings:
              .1-1.      rtAccount" means a sub-division within a fund for
      the purpose of classifying transactions •

              • 1-2.     "Agency" means a department, division, bureau,
      commission, or other organization unit of the City and County
      of Denver •
              •1-3.      71   AppropriationTT means an authorization by the City
      Council to a specified agency to expend a specified swn of money
      from a specified fund during a specified period for a specified
      purpose.

=== page 109 ===
164
              .1-4.      "Disbursement" means the paying out of cash either
      in liquidation of an expenditure or as a non-expense transaction •
              •1-5.      "Expending authority" means the officer or employe
      designated in an appropriation to approve expenditures •
              • 1-6.     "Expenditure" means a charee or obligation incurred,
      whether paid or unpaid, for the purposes of the City and County
      of Denver.       All expenditures are either "ordinary recurring ex-
      pendituresn or ttpermanent improvements" •
              . 1-7.     YTFund 11 means a sum of money or other resources
      set aside for specific purposes and constituting an independent
      fiscal and accounting entity.             A fund ordinarily has specific
      sources of receipts, specific purposes of expenditures, specific
      cash or other assets on hand, and specific liabilities.             A fund

      may be divided into two or more accounts.             The Treasury may or
      may not maintain separate bank accounts for individual funds.
      Funds are created only by Charter, state law, or ordinance •
              •1-6.      nordinary recurring expenditurett means an expendi-
      ture of a continuing or recurring character.             It includes personal
      services, contractual services, supplies, materials, debt service,
      and other similar charges •
              . 1-9.     "Permanent improvement" shall mean any acquisition
      of land, construction of or addition to buildings or other struc-
      tures, acquisition of equipment, or other expenditure for land,
      fixed improvements, or chattels, the useful life of which is ex-
      pected to be more than one year and the cost of which exceeds
      ten dollars ( ;~10. 00).       npermanent improvement" shall also mean
      an expenditure f'or a special project not of a recurring nature.

      Either construction or other projects may include expenditures
      for personal services, contractual services, supplies, or ma-
      terials.              (Sec. 2, Ord. 197, Series of 1948)

                .1.      Definition of.Cigarette.     A 11 cigaretten is any roll
      for smoking made wholly or partially of tobacco and wrapped or
      covered with paper or any other material except tobacco.                A
      cigarette may be any size or shape, and the tobacco therein may
      be adulterated or mixed with any other ingredient.                (Sec. 1,
      Ord. 49, Series of 1950)
                .2.      Definition of Package and Carton.     A "package" is
      the smallest individual box or container in which cigarettes are
      normally sold at retail.         Normally, ten such packages are con-
      tained in a "carton" container.           (Sec. 2, Ord. 49, Series of
      1950)
                .J.      Definition of Wholesale Dealer.     A nwholesale dealer"
      is any person who sells cigarettes to retail dealers or other
      persons for purposes of resale only.               (Sec. 3 , Ord. 49,
      Series of 1950)
                .4.      Definition of Retail Dealer.     A "retail dealer" is
      any person other than a wholesale dealer engaged in the business
      of selling cigarettes.             (Sec. 4, Ord. 49, Series of 1950)
                .5.      Definition of Special Stamping Privilege Dealer.
      A. ttspecial stamping privilege dealern is any person, firm, or

      corporation licensed as a retail dealer hereunder who receives
      cigarettes from sources other than a licensed wholesale dealer.
      (Sec. 5, Ord. 49, Series of 1950)

             -,.1-4( 2).   Length.    No ground sign hereafter erected or remodel-

             f.1-5.,   No Opening Between Signs; Total Length of Ad,ioining
    Signs.    There shall be no opening permitting free passage between one
    ground sign and an adjacent ground sign, whether such signs are paral-
    lel or angled to one another.         No ground sign hereafter erected or re-
    modeled and adjoined to any existing ground sign or ground signs shall
    increase the total length of such adjoining signs to more than one
    hundred feet (100') unless such signs or groups of signs are at right
    angles in relation to each other and do not exceed one hundred feet
    (100') in any direction.         Ground signs hereafter erected or remodeled
    shall be located a minimum distance of one hundred feet (100') from
    existing ground signs or groups of ground signs upon the same tract or
    parcel with unity of ownership, unless adjoined thereto in conformance
    with the one hundred {100} foot length limit provided herein, or unless
    at a right angle to each other in conformance with the requirements of
    this section.

           .1.      Flight Regulations.   It shall be unlawful for any person,
      firm, or corporation to operate or fly any airplane, aircraft, diri-
      gible, airship, free balloon, glider, helicopter, autogiro, or any
      other contrivance for flight in the air fhereinafter referred to by
      the single term naircraft") in or over the City and County of Denver,
      except in accordance with the following prescribed regulations:

           .1-1.      The operator of any aircraft shall hold a currently
      valid Airman Certificate with appropriate Airman Rating Record issued
      by the Administrator of Civil Aeronautics •
           • 1-2.     The aircraft shall carry therein a currently effective
      Aircraft Registration Certificate issued by the Administrator of
      Civil Aeronautics, and a currently effective Aircraft Airworthiness
      Certificate and Aircraft Operation Record issued by the Administrator
      of Civil Aeronautics •
           • 1-3.     All takeoffs and landings shall be made only at Stapleton
      Airfield or at other airports owned by the City and County of Denver,
      the State of Colorado, or the United States Government, or at duly
        censed aviation fields or helicopter landing areas.        No person
      shall operate any aircraft in a careless or reckless manner so as to
      endanger life or property, nor shall any person operate any aircraft
      acrobatically over any area within the City limits of the City and
      County of Denver.      The term 11 acrobaticallyn shall include any maneuver
      not necessary to maintain normal flight.       Provided 2 however, that the
  Director of Aviation may grant permission in writing for "air shows"
      over airfield property •
           • 1-4.    No person shall carry or transport in any aircraft any
      intoxicating liquor, or any narcotic drug, stimulant, or depressant,
      except as a proper part of the cargo thereof, and no person shall carry
      or transport in any such aircraft any explosive, flammable liquid,
      flammable solid, or other dangerous substance or article whatsoever
      other than that necessary for the operation of such aircraft.

           .1.   Inspectors and Meter Readers,    Any person, firm, or cor-
